rejected.statement: The holotype specimen of Isanosaurus was discovered in dark red sandstone of the Nam Phong Formation near the village of Ban Non Thaworn in Chaiyaphum Province.
rejected.quote: The specimen was found in dark red sandstone of the Nam Phong Formation near the village of Ban Non Thaworn, in Chaiyaphum Province.

rejected.statement: When discovered in 1998, the Isanosaurus skeleton had been mostly eroded away.
rejected.quote: When discovered in 1998, the skeleton had unfortunately been mostly eroded away.

rejected.statement: The genus Isanosaurus was described by French paleontologist Éric Buffetaut and colleagues in 2000.
rejected.quote: Isanosaurus was described by French palaeontologist Éric Buffetaut and colleagues in 2000.

rejected.statement: The species name attavipachi honors P. Attavipach, a supporter of paleontological research in Thailand and former Director General of the Thai Department of Mineral Resources.
rejected.quote: the species name honours P. Attavipach, a supporter of palaeontological research in Thailand and former Director General of the Thai Department of Mineral Resources.

rejected.statement: In 2026, U-Pb zircon dating confirmed that Isanosaurus lived during the Sinemurian-Pliensbachian stages of the Early Jurassic, between 197 and 192 million years ago.
rejected.quote: In 2026, U-Pb zircon dating confidently supported that the rock layers bearing the fossils of Isanosaurus were deposited during the Sinemurian-Pliensbachian (197-192 MDA) stage of the Early Jurassic.

rejected.statement: It is debated whether Isanosaurus lived during the Late Triassic or the Early Jurassic, with recent dating supporting the latter.
rejected.quote: Isanosaurus was originally thought to have lived during the Late Triassic, which would make it one of the oldest known sauropods, but other authors questioned this age estimate, suggesting that the genus lived during the Jurassic period.

rejected.statement: The only known specimen of Isanosaurus consists of a neck vertebra, a back vertebra, parts of two tail vertebrae, two chevrons, fragmentary ribs, a right sternal plate, a right shoulder blade, and a left femur.
rejected.quote: The only specimen includes a neck vertebra, a back vertebra and part of a second, six tail vertebra, two chevrons, fragmentary ribs, the right sternal plate, the right shoulder blade, and the left thigh bone (femur).

rejected.statement: The Isanosaurus individual measured approximately 6.5 meters in length, with a thigh bone measuring 76 centimeters.
rejected.quote: This individual may have measured 6.5 m when alive; the thigh bone measures 76 centimetres in length.

rejected.statement: Because the vertebral neural arches were not fused to the centra, the Isanosaurus individual was likely not fully grown.
rejected.quote: However, the vertebral neural arches have been found separated from the vertebral centra, indicating that these elements were not fused with each other; thus, this individual probably was not fully grown.

rejected.statement: Isanosaurus exhibited quadrupedal locomotion, walking on all four legs, which was an early trait among sauropods.
rejected.quote: Isanosaurus, being one of the first sauropods known, already shows a quadrupedal locomotion (with all four legs on the ground).

rejected.statement: The legs of Isanosaurus were column-like, indicated by a robust and straight thigh bone.
rejected.quote: The legs were column-like, as indicated by the robust and straight thigh bone.

rejected.statement: Like other sauropods, Isanosaurus had reduced bony processes on the femur, notably lacking the lesser trochanter.
rejected.quote: Also, like in other sauropods, bony processes of the femur were reduced in Isanosaurus; most notably, the lesser trochanter was lacking.

rejected.statement: The neck vertebrae of Isanosaurus were opisthocoelous, forming ball-and-socket joints with neighboring vertebrae.
rejected.quote: The neck vertebrae were distinctly opisthocoelous (convex at the front and hollow at the back), forming ball-and-socket joints with neighbouring vertebrae.

rejected.statement: The tail vertebrae of Isanosaurus were amphicoelous, being concave at both ends.
rejected.quote: The tail vertebrae, on the other hand, were amphicoelous (concave at both ends).

rejected.statement: The dorsal neural spines of Isanosaurus were very high, similar to those of later sauropods, unlike the low spines of prosauropods.
rejected.quote: The dorsal neural spines were very high, like those of some later sauropods, unlike the low prosauropod neural spines.

rejected.statement: The lateral sides of the Isanosaurus vertebrae were concave but not deeply excavated into pleurocoels as seen in later sauropods.
rejected.quote: The lateral sides of the vertebrae were concave, but not deeply excavated (a structure known as pleurocoels) as in later sauropods.

rejected.statement: Isanosaurus was originally classified as a sauropod but was later reidentified as a non-sauropod sauropodiform.
rejected.quote: Originally described as sauropod, it was later identified as a non-sauropod sauropodiform.

rejected.statement: Isanosaurus is a basal member of the infraorder Sauropoda, appearing more advanced than Vulcanodon, Gongxianosaurus, and Shunosaurus but less advanced than Barapasaurus.
rejected.quote: Isanosaurus es un miembro basal del infraorden Sauropoda, su relación con otros saurópodos primitivos no está bien esclarecida, al parecer es más avanzado que Vulcanodon, Gongxianosaurus y Shunosaurus pero menos que Barapasaurus.

rejected.statement: Isanosaurus lived during the Late Triassic, approximately between 214 and 201 million years ago, in what is now Asia.
rejected.quote: que vivió a finales del período Triásico, hace aproximadamente entre 214 a 201 millones de años, desde el Noriense al Rhaetiense, en lo que es hoy Asia.

rejected.statement: The Paleobiology Database records the time range of Isanosaurus as Pliensbachian to Toarcian, from 192.9 to 174.7 million years ago.
rejected.quote: Time range: Pliensbachian to Toarcian (192.9 to 174.7 million years ago)
